page_title: WolfClip — clipboard history for Mac and Linux

summary.name: WolfClip
summary.one_liner: WolfClip is a free, open-source clipboard history manager for macOS and Linux that pastes a picked item straight into the app you were using, with a Win+V-style shortcut.
use_cases: Recall text, links, code or images copied earlier
Pasting frequently used addresses, snippets or templates
Replacing Windows-style Win+V history on a Mac
Keeping clipboard history private on a local machine
Clipboard history on Linux under X11 or Wayland
summary.what_it_does: WolfClip records what you copy (text, links, colors, code, images and Finder files) and shows it in a history list. Pressing ⇧⌘V on macOS (or Super+V on Linux under X11) opens the list, and selecting an item pastes it into the app you were typing in. You can search by typing, filter by type, and use ⌘1–⌘9 to pick the first nine items. Pinned items stay on top and never expire. Items marked as secret by password managers are skipped, and history is stored as a local file. The macOS app checks GitHub Releases for updates and can be turned off in Settings.
notable: Win+V-style flow: one shortcut, pick an item, it is pasted into the current app
Pins never expire and sit at the top of history
Skips passwords marked concealed or transient by password managers; history stays on the local machine
Native Swift/SwiftUI on macOS and GTK 4 on Linux, no Electron
caveats: macOS build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple; Gatekeeper may need manual approval unless installed via Homebrew
Linux Wayland support is in beta and auto-paste needs wtype or ydotool
Requires macOS 14 or later; Windows is not a supported platform
